title: Predictive slot rebalancer: session-aware eviction and graceful fallback
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem:
We continue to see tenant-level connection saturation events in high-variance workloads (bursting chatbots and periodic embedding ingestion), which produce cascading increases in downstream latency (redis/kafka) and localized P99 spikes. Current connpool eviction is reactive and coarse-grained: when global connection budgets are exhausted we close arbitrary idle connections, which can break session affinity and cause amplified retry storms.

Goal:
1) Reduce tenant-visible outage windows and connection saturation-induced P99 tail spikes.
2) Provide graceful, predictable degradation for tenants when downstream stores are constrained (Redis, Kafka, SQL).
3) Keep changes safe to roll out multi-region with per-region control and observability.

Design summary (high level):
- Predictive slot rebalancer: a controller that tracks per-session and per-tenant connection usage with short EWMA activity scores and predicts likely active sessions for the next 60s window.
- Session-aware eviction: instead of LRU only, eviction prefers connections with low EWMA scores and no affinity metadata; keep at-least-one-hot active path for heavy sessions.
- Tiered fallback behaviors:
  * Tier 0 (healthy): normal pooling and autoscale.
  * Tier 1 (constrained): soft-evict idle slots, enable read-sloppy mode for non-critical reads (serve cached Redis snapshots), and enable short-lived hedging for requests hitting downstream.
  * Tier 2 (degraded): collapse to shared pooled read-only proxies (cached responses / precomputed summaries), reject low-priority background jobs with 429, and route heavy real-time sessions to regional fallback model variants that use less downstream pressure.
- Multi-region rebalancing: local controller runs per-region; global coordinator can instruct asymmetric policies for region-to-region failovers.
- Circuit breaker integration: upstream request router observes rebalancer signals and downstream error rates to open per-tenant circuit breakers with semantically meaningful reasons (e.g., REDIS_HIGH_LATENCY, KAFKA_BACKPRESSURE).

Implementation notes:
- EWMA parameters tuned to emphasize short bursts (alpha ~ 0.35 for 1 minute horizon).
- Maintain per-tenant slot assignment table in an in-memory sharded store (bounded size) with TTL; persist sampling traces to Kafka for offline tuning.
- New connpool API flags: session_id (optional), affinity_hint (enum), priority (P0..P3). Backwards compatible default behavior if flags omitted.
- Safety nets: when rebalancer is in error state or telemetry missing, controller falls back to current LRU eviction logic.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary on infra team services (5% traffic) for 48h. Monitor connection saturation events and tail-latency.
2) Gradual ramp to 25% with opt-out switch per-tenant.
3) Full enable in staging followed by progressive region rollouts.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- New metrics: per-tenant conn_utilization, predicted_active_fraction, evictions_per_minute, downstream_miss_rate, degraded_responses_ratio.
- Alerts: conn_utilization > 85% AND evictions_per_minute > baseline -> page ops.
- Acceptance criteria:
  * Reduce number of saturation-triggered P99 spikes by >= 40% in canary tenants over baseline.
  * No more than 3 tenant-facing 5xx spikes during canary window.
  * Ability to disable feature per-tenant within 30s.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should session stickiness be to avoid starving new sessions? (we propose a minimum slot fraction per-tenant)
- Cost of maintaining per-session state vs benefits — we will simulate using production traffic traces before full rollout.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing SDKs will continue to work. New affinity flags are additive. DevX to publish migration notes and example usage.

Documentation and runbook:
- Confluence design doc above includes operator runbook for handling false positives during canary.
- Runbook snippets: emergency-disable path, metrics to check (connpool heatmap, redis latency, kafka queue depth), rollback to LRU.

Acceptance Criteria (explicit):
- Implementation merged and passes unit + integration tests.
- Canary run (5% traffic) for 48h with metrics meeting acceptance criteria.
- Documentation and DevX blog + SDK examples published.
- Postmortem template ready in case of regressions.
comments: 2026-01-18 - Triage: found recurring tenant saturation reports in January incidents; Lena created ticket and attached initial traces.

2026-01-25 - Design kickoff: architecture review with infra, runtime, and platform teams. Decided EWMA approach and three-tier degradation model. Action: Mateo to prototype rebalancer shim in staging.

2026-02-04 - Proto status: initial prototype implemented that emits predicted_active_fraction and supports session_id hint. Observed lower evictions in synthetic burst test. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428.

2026-02-16 - Code review: infra requested additional telemetry, and QA flagged a regression where affinity hinted connections were sometimes closed by LRU. Patch submitted to respect affinity until soft-eviction threshold.
2026-02-22 - Load test: 48h synthetic burst run in staging showed 37% reduction in saturation-triggered P99 spikes (just below our 40% target). Decided to tweak EWMA alpha and rerun.
2026-03-03 - Pre-canary: metrics pipeline and dashboards instrumented; per-tenant opt-out toggle implemented in Console. Ops runbook drafted.

2026-03-08 - Canary started (5% infra traffic): initial 6h window looks stable, slight increase in evictions_per_minute but downstream_miss_rate unchanged. Monitoring page configured for 24/7 watch during first 48h.
Action items: finalize EWMA tuning after 24h canary, prepare communications for customers for next ramp.
